WITHOUT IMPOSING ANY TOLLS, IN LINE WITH THE OUTCOMES 
AND EFFORTS REACHED BY THE UNITED STATES AND ISLAMIC 
REPUBLIC OF IRAN.
2. THE SULTANATE OF OMAN HAS WORKED IN COORDINATION WITH
THE INTERNATIONAL MARITIME ORGANIZATION (IMO) TO PROVIDE
ALL VESSELS WITH THE OPTION OF A TEMPORARY MARITIME 
CORRIDOR DEFINED BY THE COORDINATES LISTED BELOW.
3. THE SAFETY OF NAVIGATION REMAINS THE PARAMOUNT CONSIDERATION.
GIVEN THE ELEVATED RISK OF COLLISION IN THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT,
A GRADUAL AND CONTROLLED EVACUATION OF VESSEL TRAFFIC IS REQUIRED.
4. TO MITIGATE THESE RISKS, THE IMO HAS DEVELOPED A PHASED 
APPROACH BASED ON GROUPS OF VESSELS WITH THE FULL COORDINATION
OF THE OMANI AUTHORITIES.
5. CURRENT REPORTS INDICATE THAT THE TSS IS NOT SAFE FOR USE AT
THIS TIME. BASED ON AVAILABLE INFORMATION FROM THE IMO, TWO 
TEMPORARY ROUTES MAY BE UTILIZED BY VESSELS DEPARTING THROUGH
THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ: ONE SOUTH OF THE EXISTING TRAFFIC 
SEPARATION SCHEME (TSS) AND ONE TO THE NORTH.
6. VESSELS INCLUDED IN THE DESIGNATED GROUPS WILL BE CONTACTED 
INDIVIDUALLY AND PROVIDED WITH FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING 
THEIR DEPARTURE BY RELEVANT PARTIES COORDINATED BY THE IMO.

AND ADVISED OF THEIR ALLOCATED TRANSIT DAY BY THE PARTIES COORDINATED
BY IMO.

THE DESIGNATED WAITING AREA WITHIN INTERNATIONAL WATERS, 
WITHIN A 3 NM RADIUS OF POSITION 26-16.17N/055-46.52E.

In de volgende gebieden op de Westerschelde zijn locaties aangewezen voor het gebruik van spudpalen: 5.1.1. Vaarwater langs Hoofdplaat 5.1.2. Everingen Zuid zijde 5.1.3. Middelgat 5.1.4. Voorschriften voor gebruik van ankergebieden Westerschelde en haar mondingen 6.1. Alle vaartuigen mogen pas ankeren na verkregen toestemming van de GNA. De toestemming kan door de GNA via de desbetreffende verkeerscentrale worden gegeven. Aan de toestemming kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden. 6.2. Voorschriften van toepassing op alle schepen: a. Binnen de begrenzing van de ankergebieden Westhinder, Oostdyck en Schouwenbank kan zelf een ankerplaats worden gekozen. Voordat het schip het anker laat vallen, zal de positie moeten worden goedgekeurd door de desbetreffende verkeerscentrale. b. In ankergebieden Wielingen Noord, Wielingen Zuid en Vlissingen Rede is het ten anker liggen onder normale omstandigheden gelimiteerd tot maximaal 24 uur. c. Voor werkzaamheden op de ankerplaatsen dient toestemming en/of een vergunning te worden aangevraagd volgens onderstaande methoden: 1) Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale voor de ankergebieden Westhinder, Oostdyck en Schouwenbank. 2) Via het havensysteem Enigma+ voor de Everingen positie A t/m E en de Put van Terneuzen positie A en B. 3) Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale in de gebieden voor overslag werkzaamheden van zand en grind. Dit staat beschreven in artikel 10 van deze GB. 4) Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale of per email via de GNA voor de nog niet benoemde gebieden in dit artikel. d. Het is verboden om spudpalen te gebruiken in de aangewezen ankergebieden, tenzij het ankergebied tevens is aangewezen als gebied voor het gebruik van spudpalen. 6.3. Voorschriften van toepassing op gastankers of geladen met gevaarlijke stoffen: a. Voor gastankers waarop de GB “Vervoer van gevaarlijke stoffen in gastankers binnen het GNB- gebied” van toepassing is geldt het volgende indien de reis van een Vaarplan IMO 2 Gastanker om enige reden zou moeten worden onderbroken: 1) Het schip moet ten anker komen op een door de GNA aangewezen ankerplaats. 2) Voor een schip met bestemming of komend van Zeebrugge zal een aanbevolen ankerplaats worden toegewezen. Indien er een loods aan boord is wordt de ankerplaats toegewezen door de VC Zeebrugge in samenspraak met de GNA en de bedienende loods. Indien er geen loods aan boord is wijst VC Zeebrugge het ankergebied Westhinder aan. 3) Voor een schip met een andere bestemming binnen het GNB-gebied zal deze ten anker komen in een bij voorkeur zo westelijk mogelijke positie in ankergebied Wielingen Noord of indien beschikbaar ankerplaats Everingen Alfa. b. Schepen die geladen zijn met gevaarlijke stoffen genoemd in bijlage 1 van het SRW mogen enkel ankeren in de ankergebieden Westhinder en Schouwenbank. In geval van overmacht kan er met toestemming van de GNA zo westelijk mogelijk geankerd worden in ankergebied Wielingen Noord. c. Schepen met een lengte ≤ 110 m die geladen zijn met gevaarlijke stoffen genoemd in bijlage 1 van het SRW (niet zijnde gevaarlijke stoffen genoemd onder SRW bijlage 1, lid 1 en 2), mogen met toestemming van de GNA ankeren in ankergebied Vlissingen Rede oostelijk deel (‘driehoek’). Dit enkel in geval van bezwaren van nautische of meteorologische aard. Artikel 7. Voorschriften voor gebruik van ankergebieden Beneden-Zeeschelde 7.1. Aan de toestemming kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden. 7.2. De GNA bepaalt de locatie waar en de voorwaarden waaronder een vaartuig kan ankeren. 7.3. Voor werkzaamheden op de ankerplaatsen dient toestemming en/of een vergunning te worden aangevraagd volgens onderstaande methoden: a. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale of per email via de GNA. b. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale in de gebieden voor overslag werkzaamheden van zand en grind. Dit staat beschreven in artikel 10 van deze GB. 7.4. Het is verboden om spudpalen te gebruiken in de aangewezen ankergebieden, tenzij het ankergebied tevens is aangewezen als gebied voor het gebruik van spudpalen. Artikel 8. Voorschriften voor gebruik van spudpalen in de aangewezen gebieden op de Westerschelde en Beneden-Zeeschelde 8.1. Alle vaartuigen mogen gebruik maken van hun spudpalen na verkregen toestemming van de GNA. Aan de toestemming kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden. 8.2. De GNA bepaalt de locatie waar en de voorwaarden waaronder een vaartuig gebruik kan maken van spudpalen. 8.3. Wanneer het desbetreffende schip op haar spudpalen ligt wordt dit gemeld aan de desbetreffende verkeerscentrale. 8.4. Niets ontheft hierbij de gezagvoerder van het lopen van ankerwacht conform de huidige wet- en regelgeving. Daarbij is het verplicht om te alle tijden uit te luisteren op het juiste VHF verkeerskanaal. 8.5. Voor werkzaamheden in de aangewezen gebieden voor het gebruik van spudpalen dient toestemming en/of een vergunning te worden aangevraagd volgens onderstaande methoden: a. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale of per email via de GNA. b. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale in de gebieden voor overslag werkzaamheden van zand en grind. Dit staat beschreven in artikel 10 van deze GB. Artikel 9. Ankeren van schepen met schade na een incident 9.1. Schepen die na een incident schade of vermoedelijke schade hebben opgelopen mogen hun reis naar hun eindbestemming slechts voortzetten na toestemming van de GNA. 9.2. De schepen dienen in principe eerst ten anker te komen op een door de GNA aangewezen ankerplaats alwaar een eerste onderzoek naar de aard van de schade wordt uitgevoerd. 9.3. Bij een incident moet onderstaande wetgeving in acht worden genomen: - KB houdende politie- en scheepvaartreglement voor de Belgische territoriale zee, de havens en de stranden van de Belgische kust (1981), artikel 27 en 29. - KB houdende scheepvaartreglement voor de Beneden-Zeeschelde (1992), artikel 44 en 47. - Scheepvaartreglement Westerschelde 1990, artikel 51 en 54. - Scheepvaartreglement voor het Kanaal van Gent naar Terneuzen, artikel 43 en 53. - KB houdende Scheepvaartreglement voor het Kanaal van Gent naar Terneuzen (1992), artikel 43 en 52. - Havenpolitieverordening Haven van Antwerpen (2024), artikel 8.1.4 lid 1. - Havenverordening North Sea Port 2025 (Gemeente Vlissingen, Borsele en Terneuzen), artikel 3.9. - Havenpolitieverordening North Sea Port Gent (2026), artikel 3.2.1. Artikel 10. Overslag van zeezand en grind 10.1. De overslag van zeezand en grind is enkel toegestaan op de door de GNA aangewezen gebieden en onder bepaalde voorwaarden. Dit wordt nader geregeld middels een GB (of een Bass). Artikel 11. Bijzondere omstandigheden en uitzonderingen 11.1. Afhankelijk van de omstandigheden, technische mogelijkheden, scheepstypen, soort lading of verkeerssituatie kan de Gemeenschappelijke Nautische Autoriteit extra voorschriften vaststellen dan wel afwijken en/of uitzonderingen maken van/op deze voorschriften. 1.The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) notes in past marine incidents the need for crew familiarization with shipboard equipment and systems.
2.This Marine Notice wishes to make recommendations to all Shipowners & operators having large fleets for the need to establish dedicated onshore or fleet-based training workshops specifically for crew trainings and practices. These workshops will boost crew familiarity, hands-on safety drill practice, and operational readiness for onboard equipment and systems.
3.Be advised that the Maritime Transport Act 2013 and the Maritime (STCW Convention) Regulations 2014 highlights the need for crew familiarization with critical shipboard equipment, bridge systems, safety gear, and emergency appliances through continuous practical training as it would enhance maritime safety and the protection of the marine environment.
4.For any clarification, please contact the undersigned.
SAVENACA CAVALEVU
EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN (MSAF)
Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji
22nd October 2026

1.This Marine Notice serves to remind all Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents of the importance of maintaining order and discipline of all persons on board ships to protect safety of life at sea and ensure lawful crew management.
2.With recent cases on the above subject matter, the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) would like to remind all Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents of the Master’s duty to have the final authority to control the ship while in command and for the discipline of all persons on board.
3.Additionally, Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents are reminded to ensure that disciplinary procedures are implemented as part of the Safe Ship Management System for the Company and also onboard its ships.
4.This Notice serves to give notice that any misconduct affecting the safe operation of the ships, repeated disregard of lawful safety requirements or instructions, or misconduct contributing to any accident, incident or mishap should be reported to the MSAF. Any such recurring records against a seafarer will engage the enforcement measures of MSAF.

The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) wishes to advise all shipowners, ship operators, Masters and Maritime stakeholders of the servicing facility currently approved by the Authority to undertake the servicing of inflatable liferafts in Fiji.
This Marine Notice is issued to ensure that inflatable liferafts carried on vessels are serviced by an MSAF-approved servicing station and within the approved scope of the facility.
Approved Liferaft Servicing Station
Facility: Liferaft Sales and Service Centre (Fiji) Pte Limited.
Location: Corner of Renown Street and Rodwell Road, Suva.
MSAF Statement of Compliance: LRSC 01/2026.
The facility has been assessed and approved by MSAF in accordance with regulation 10.4 Paragraph 10 of the Maritime (Fiji Maritime Code) Regulations 2014.

The specific Liferaft types and models covered by the facility approval are provided in Appendix A to this Marine Notice.
Advice to Shipowners and Operators
•Ensure liferaft are serviced at the required intervals.
•Ensure servicing is undertaken by an MSAF-approved servicing station.
•Confirm that the servicing station is authorised to service the particular make, type and model of liferaft presented.
•Retain servicing documentation and make it available during MSAF surveys and inspections.
•Do not accept servicing or certification of liferaft that fall outside the approved scope of the servicing station.
Where a liferaft make or model is not listed in Appendix A, shipowners and operators are advised to contact MSAF before making servicing arrangements. MSAF will advise the maritime industry through appropriate notices should additional servicing stations or liferaft brands be approved.

w.id: Hong Kong Coastal Hong Kong MDN 214/2026
w.t:
MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 214/2026 (Navigation Warnings & Related Information)
Cross Harbour Swimming Races and Closure of Landing Steps
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that swimming races across the Central Harbour from Wan Chai, Hong Kong Island to Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon will take place from 0700 hours to 1100 hours on 15 November 2026. About 4,000 swimmers, under the escort of guard boats, are expected to participate in the races.
2. Launches of the Marine Department and Marine Police will be stationed or patrolling in the Central Harbour before and during the event.
3. Masters, coxswains and persons-in-charge of all vessels navigating in the vicinity should proceed with caution and give a wide berth to the swimmers, and follow the directions given by officers on Marine Department and Marine Police launches regulating marine traffic in the vicinity.
4. As the marine traffic in the Central Harbour will be affected by the races, vessel operators are advised to adjust their sailing schedules in order to avoid obstructing the races.
5. To facilitate the event, the following landing steps will be temporarily closed:
(i) Public Landings at the starting/finishing points – from 0900 hours on 14 November 2026 to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026;
(ii) Kowloon Public Pier No. 1 – from 0900 hours on 14 November 2026 to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026; and
(iii) Kowloon Public Pier No. 2 to No. 4 – from 0500 hours to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026.
6. During the aforementioned closure periods, owners and coxswains of vessels are advised to use other landing facilities in the vicinity.
7. A drawing showing the route of the races and the affected landing step is attached to this Notice.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine
Marine Department Government of the HKSAR Date: 10 November 2026 Action File Ref.: L/M 704/26 in MD-HPS-F01-015-045-002

w.t:
MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 85/2026 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring “B” mooring A17, A29, A35, B2, B4 A36, A38, A39, A43, A78
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. Further information on minimum safe manning levels on ships while in the waters of Hong Kong can be found in Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/proc/index.html)
8. Coxswains, owners, agents and persons in control of local vessels are advised to take the precautionary measures contained in the Marine Department pamphlet entitled “Measures to Enhance the Safety of Local Vessels During Passage of Tropical Cyclones” well before a tropical cyclone is approaching Hong Kong. The pamphlet is available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/publication/materials/pdf/hps_cyclones.pdf)
9. This Notice supersedes Marine Department Notice No. 60 of 2025.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine

MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 41/2026 (Marine Works)
Improvement Works at Yung Shue O Jetty
With immediate effect and for a period of approximately 21 months, improvement works for the jetty will be carried out within the area bounded by straight lines joining the following co-ordinates (WGS 84 Datum) from (A) to (F) and the adjacent shoreline:
(A) 22-25.17N 114-16.65E (B) 22-25.18N 114-16.62E (C) 22-25.21N 114-16.64E (D) 22-25.20N 114-16.65E (E) 22-25.23N 114-16.67E (F) 22-25.20N 114-16.72E
2. The works will be carried out by two dumb lighters and one pilling barge. One roro barge, one tugboat and one work boat will provide assistance. Vessels engaged in the works will display signals as prescribed in international and local regulations.
3. The hours of work will be from 0700 to 1900 hours. No works will be carried out on Sundays and public holidays. Vessels employed for the works will stay in the works area outside the hours of work.
4. A working area of approximately 20 metres around the working vessels will be established. Yellow marker buoys fitted with yellow flashing lights will be laid to mark the positions of the anchors extending from the working vessels.
5. Silt curtains, which are large pieces of netting to contain mud and sediments extending from the sea surface to the seabed, will be established within the works area. Yellow marker buoys fitted with yellow flashing lights will be laid to mark the extent of the silt curtains.
6. Diving operations will be carried out from time to time during the hours of work. Vessels navigating in the vicinity should proceed with caution and keep clear of the works area at slow speed, bearing in mind that there are divers working in the area.
7. A drawing showing the works area is attached to this Notice.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine

w.t:
MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 60/2025 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring “B” mooring A17, A36, A43 B03, B04 A74, A77
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 71/2024 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring
“B” mooring A17, A36, A73 B03, B30 A74, A77, A78
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. Further information on minimum safe manning levels on ships while in the waters of Hong Kong can be found in Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/proc/index.html)
8. Coxswains, owners, agents and persons in control of local vessels are advised to take the precautionary measures contained in the Marine Department pamphlet entitled “Measures to Enhance the Safety of Local Vessels During Passage of Tropical Cyclones” well before a tropical cyclone is approaching Hong Kong. The pamphlet is available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/publication/materials/pdf/hps_cyclones.pdf)
9. This Notice supersedes Marine Department Notice No. 77 of 2023.
